title: OSHA Scaffold Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.451)
subtitle: For the competent person's check before each shift and after anything that may have affected the scaffold's structure.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item fails, keep employees off the affected part until it is repaired, replaced or braced, or until the scaffold is removed from service.
The scaffold manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Foundation, bracing and capacity
items: Scaffold built and loaded as the qualified person's design specifies
Workers and materials within the maximum intended load or rated capacity, whichever is less
Every pole, leg, post, frame and upright bears on base plates and mud sills or other adequate firm foundation
Level, sound and rigid, with no settling or displacement under the loaded scaffold
No unstable objects supporting the scaffold or platform units
Uprights plumb, bracing in place, no swaying or displacement
Scaffold taller than 4 times its base width is guyed, tied or braced

Vertical tie positions follow the manufacturer's recommendations, or start at the 4:1 height and repeat every 20 ft or less (3 ft wide or less) or 26 ft or less (wider). In all cases: ties at each end, no more than 30 ft apart horizontally, and the top tie no further than the 4:1 height from the top
At least 10 ft from insulated lines of 300 V to 50 kV and uninsulated lines under 50 kV, at least 3 ft from insulated lines under 300 V, and more for lines over 50 kV
No damaged or weakened part in use unless repaired, replaced or braced to the strength required by (a)

sections.title: Platforms
items: Each working level fully planked or decked between front uprights and guardrail supports
No more than 1 in between units and between platform and uprights (where a wider space has been justified, no more than 9 1/2 in)
At least 18 in wide, or the width (b)(2)(i) or (b)(2)(ii) allows
Front edge within 14 in of the work face, or guardrails or fall arrest in use along it. Outrigger scaffolds: no more than 3 in from the face. Plastering and lathing: no more than 18 in
Each end at least 6 in past the support centerline, or cleated or hooked
Platforms 10 ft or shorter overhang no more than 12 in unless designed for it or guarded against access
Overlaps only over supports, at least 12 in, or nailed or restrained
No debris building up on platforms
No snow, ice or other slippery material, except while workers are removing it
No boxes, barrels or other makeshift devices used to gain working height

sections.title: Access
items: Ladder, stair tower, ramp, walkway, integral access or direct access wherever the platform is over 2 ft above or below the access point
Nobody climbing cross braces on tubular welded frame scaffolds
Portable, hook-on and attachable ladders placed so they cannot tip the scaffold
Hook-on or attachable ladder bottom rung no more than 24 in above the supporting level
Rest platforms at 35 ft maximum vertical intervals on supported scaffolds over 35 ft high
Toprail and midrail on each side of each scaffold stairway
Guardrails on ramps and walkways 6 ft or more above lower levels
Scaffold no more than 14 in horizontally and 24 in vertically from the other surface

sections.title: Fall and falling object protection
items: Every employee over 10 ft up is protected by the system (g)(1)(i) to (g)(1)(vii) requires for this scaffold type
Guardrails on all open sides and ends before anyone other than erection or dismantling crews uses the scaffold
38 to 45 in above the platform (36 to 45 in on supported scaffolds made and placed in service before January 1, 2000, and on suspended scaffolds needing both guardrail and fall arrest)
Midrail approximately midway between top edge and platform
No steel or plastic banding used as toprail or midrail
Lanyard attached to a vertical lifeline, horizontal lifeline or scaffold structural member
At least three and one-half in high at the outermost edge, no more than 1/4 in gap above the surface, openings no larger than 1 in
Area below barricaded with no entry, or another (h)(2) measure in place where objects could strike employees below
Hardhats worn on the scaffold, plus toeboards, screens, guardrails, nets, catch platforms or canopies against small falling objects

sections.title: Inspection, supervision and conditions
items: Competent person checked for visible defects before this shift and after any event that may have affected the structure
Erecting, moving, dismantling or altering supervised by a competent person and done by trained, experienced employees that person selected
No work in storms or high winds unless a competent person found it safe and workers have fall arrest or wind screens, with the scaffold secured for wind forces
Tag lines or equivalent control on loads hoisted onto or near the scaffold
Ropes inspected by a competent person this workshift, with none showing a replacement condition in (d)(10)(i) to (d)(10)(vi)
Counterweights of non-flowable material, with no sand, gravel or similar easily dislocated material
Only items specifically designed as counterweights, with no masonry units, rolls of roofing felt or other construction materials
Counterweights secured to the outrigger beams by mechanical means
Tiebacks secured to structurally sound anchorage, not standpipes, vents, piping or electrical conduit

references: 29 CFR 1926.451: General requirements (Part 1926 Subpart L: Scaffolds)
Aerial lifts are covered by 29 CFR 1926.453, not this section
